tool.name: roast
tool.description: : reference-guided multiple alignment of pairwise MAFs (multiz autoMZ)
tool.command: ## Galaxy flattens newlines in <command>, so the work is a POSIX sh script (the multiz image is BusyBox). sh '$script'

configfiles.configfile: #set $names = [str($m.element_identifier) for $m in $pairwise] set -eu ref='$reference' case "\$ref" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) echo "reference name must be letters, digits or _: \$ref" >&2; exit 1;; esac mkdir work ## UCSC's tree preparation (kent src/hg/makeDb/doc/hg38/multiz5way.txt): branch lengths, the ';' and ## newlines go, commas become spaces: ((hg38 (tupChi1 galVar1)) (mm10 cavPor3)). tree=\$(sed 's/:[-0-9.eE]*//g; s/;//; /^ *\$/d' '$tree' | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ //g; s/,/ /g') species=\$(echo "\$tree" | tr '()' ' ') echo " \$species " | grep -q " \$ref " || { echo "reference \$ref is not in the tree" >&2; exit 1; } #for $m in $pairwise name='$m.element_identifier' case "\$name" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) echo "element identifier must be letters, digits or _: \$name" >&2; exit 1;; esac echo " \$species " | grep -q " \$name " || { echo "\$name is not in the tree" >&2; exit 1; } if [ -s '$m' ]; then ln -s '$m' "work/\$ref.\$name.sing.maf"; else echo '\#\#maf version=1 scoring=autoMZ' > "work/\$ref.\$name.sing.maf"; fi #end for ## a species in the tree with no alignment in this piece gets UCSC's empty stub (autoMultiz.csh) for s in \$species; do [ "\$s" = "\$ref" ] && continue [ -e "work/\$ref.\$s.sing.maf" ] || echo '\#\#maf version=1 scoring=autoMZ' > "work/\$ref.\$s.sing.maf" done echo "tree: \$tree" cd work mkdir tmp roast + T="\$PWD/tmp" E="\$ref" "\$tree" \$ref.*.sing.maf out.maf > /dev/null mv out.maf '$output'

param.name: pairwise
param.label: Pairwise MAFs, one per species
param.help: Each element's identifier is the species name used in its MAF rows (e.g. mm10 for rows named mm10.chr1); the reference is the top row of every block, and each file is sorted by reference position.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference name
param.help: As it prefixes the reference rows (hg38 for hg38.chr1). Letters, digits and _ only.

param.name: tree
param.label: Species tree
param.help: Newick; branch lengths are ignored. Every species (and the reference) must be a leaf.

reference mm39 is not in the tree

tool.help:
**What it does**
Runs ``roast`` (multiz's ``autoMZ``) over one set of pairwise MAFs that share a reference, as UCSC's ``autoMultiz.csh`` does for each piece of a multizNway build:
::
autoMZ + T=$tmp E=$db "`cat tree.nh`" $db.*.sing.maf $c
Each input becomes ``<reference>.<species>.sing.maf``. A species in the tree with no input, or an empty one, gets UCSC's stub ``##maf version=1 scoring=autoMZ``, so one piece of a genome split can be run without every species aligning to it.
The tree is prepared as UCSC does: branch lengths, ``;`` and newlines are removed and commas become spaces, giving ``((hg38 (tupChi1 galVar1)) (mm10 cavPor3))``. UCSC's scripts also strip a lowercase ``name_`` prefix, which exists for their common-name trees; it is not applied here, because the leaves must be the species names the MAF rows use.
.. warning:: Pairwise inputs must be sorted by reference position. multiz merges unsorted input wrongly with exit status 0. ``netToAxt | axtSort | axtToMaf`` (or ``mafSplit`` of such a file) gives the right order.
**Output** is roast's MAF: header ``##maf version=1 scoring=roast.v3.3``, blocks with the reference on top, and a final ``##eof maf``. Gap annotation (``mafAddIRows``) is a separate, per-sequence step.
.. _multiz: https://github.com/multiz/multiz
